Sofia / Tom — I reviewed Clinical Fusion's redlines (v3). Below are proposed redline approaches and open items for negotiation:

Option A — Operational clause (preferred for lower legal friction):
- Add an "Evidence Runbook" exhibit to the Order Form that defines snapshot cadence, witness process, and roles.
- Redwood retains custody of snapshots for the witness window only; Helion receives a signed manifest and SHA256 hash at creation.
- Remote witness: 72-hour access window via a read-only console with session recording; on-site witness requires 30 days' notice and mutually agreeable dates.

Option B — Escrow-style deposit (stronger for Helion, more contract work):
- Provide a time-limited deposit model where Redwood deposits an encrypted snapshot with a named third-party escrow agent after the initial 6-month period.
- Key custody: Helion can require escrowed key release under narrowly defined triggers (degradation, failure to meet SLA, insolvency).

Open items / requested clarifications:
- Define the exact retention period and who pays storage costs for escrowed artifacts.
- Reconcile license scope language: if Redwood provides a deposit to a third party that includes model artifacts, we need explicit limited-use clauses to prevent derivative rights.

I can draft both exhibit options. Aditya — pls confirm whether pricing/Order Form needs a one-time escrow setup fee or whether we absorb initial setup in the current commercial terms for HLN-2028-0457.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: PrivDeploy addendum — proposed evidence handback cadence and operator scope

Quick ops notes (technical constraints / suggestions):

- Snapshot size & frequency: monthly sealed snapshots for a large model + data set can be multi-TB. If Helion wants monthly for 6 months, we should confirm network egress window and whether Helion will accept incremental deltas (KV + weights diff) instead of full images to reduce transfer and storage cost.

- Sealed snapshot definition: we can provide a signed manifest + either (1) a Redwood-hosted encrypted object in Helion storage (Helion keys) or (2) Redwood-hosted encrypted object (Redwood keys) with split-key escrow. Option (1) keeps custody with Helion and is lower risk.

- Witnessing: remote witness via read-only console is straightforward. On-site witness requires runbook for privileged access and a scoped test harness — estimate 2-3 days ops prep and an on-site security engineer.

Attachments: snapshot-procedure-diagram.png (shows delta vs full snapshot flow)

If Helion prefers the escrow agent route, we should add a one-time operational onboarding sprint of ~5 engineer-days to set up split-key escrow, manifests, and CI to generate signed proofs.

-Jonas
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the two-option approach — that helps. Clinical Fusion's counsel prefers Option B (escrow-style) but will consider Option A if Redwood accepts the following edits:

- Redwood to deposit an encrypted snapshot (or incremental delta) with a named neutral escrow agent after each of the first two monthly snapshots; thereafter quarterly until year-end.
- Redwood bears escrow setup cost; Helion pays ongoing storage after the first 90 days.
- Model artifact use restriction: escrowed artifacts may be used only for verification/witnessing and not for model training, derivative services, or benchmarking; explicit injunctive remedies for breach.

Next steps:
1) Laura — can you circulate a short draft Exhibit (escrow deposit flow + triggers + cost allocation) that we can redline?
2) Jonas — please add an ops estimate for the 5 engineer-days for escrow onboarding into the exhibit or a short SOW.
3) Aditya/Sofia — ping us with a proposed timeline for the DocuSign/Order Form update.

We attached a suggested list of neutral escrow agents in the original packet; happy to share again. Thanks — looking forward to the draft exhibit.

Tom
